note: Single source of truth for what this project claims and what backs each claim. tools/verify_claims.py checks every number here against the run records and renders CLAIMS.md. Status values: known = prior result, cited, not claimed as new; checked = numerical check passes and a reference proof exists (AI-drafted; the author's own proof is pending); exploratory = runs exist but are few-seed and not pre-registered; fails = the stated test fails as written; untested = no evidence yet.

claims.statement: Executed interventions on groups of at most k agents identify every dividend up to order k exactly.
claims.formula: m(T) = sum over R inside T of (-1)^(|T|-|R|) v(R)

claims.statement: Branches sampled from the Shapley kernel identify the Shapley value itself (Lundberg and Lee 2017; FastSHAP's objective). Used, not claimed.
claims.formula: phi = argmin of the kernel-weighted least-squares fit, subject to efficiency

claims.statement: Credit fitted on the team's own data converges to a policy-weighted Banzhaf index, not to responsibility. The closed form is known (Hammer and Holzman 1992; Grabisch, Marichal and Roubens 2000; Ding et al. 2008); its reading as multi-agent credit is this project's.
claims.formula: beta_i = sum over T containing i of m(T) * prod over j in T, j != i of p_j

claims.statement: An order-k readout errs by exactly the dropped higher-order tail, at most the tail mass divided by k + 1.
claims.formula: |phi_i - readout_i| <= sum over T containing i, |T| > k of |m(T)| / (k + 1)

claims.statement: Branch-design law: per unit sigma^2 / B the noise factor is 4 at order 1, 4 (n - 2)^2 for order-2 small groups and (sqrt Z + 2/n)^2 for the kernel design, Z = 2 (n - 1) H(n - 1) / n. At eight agents: 144 against 5.7.
Additive on-policy credit favours the weaker of two agents that share a synergy kappa by kappa (p_strong - p_weak). Responsibility from executed branches has no such gap.
claims.formula: gap = kappa * (p_s - p_w) * prod of the other members' competences

claims.statement: Two teams can produce identical logs and have different responsibility. Attribution from logs alone is not identified.
If an agent can tell an audit branch from the real run with probability delta, it shifts delta R / 2 of its blame onto an honest agent at no cost on the real path.
If audit branches are indistinguishable up to delta, no strategy shifts more than 2 R delta. Tight up to a factor of 4.
On planted games (4 agents, order 3, 3 seeds) the executed-branch critic keeps improving with budget; the on-policy additive model stops near its bias.

Level-Based Foraging, scripted team, 20-step window: the amortised critic beats a 32-branch Monte Carlo estimate on all 3 seeds. With a one-step intervention nothing beats predicting zero. Re-run on 11 Nov 2026 from commit 4c3326e with machine-written records: identical to every reported digit.
claims.formula: gate condition 3: critic error < 32-branch Monte Carlo error

claims.statement: RobotWarehouse, scripted team, 10-step window: the amortised critic loses to 32-branch Monte Carlo on all 3 seeds, even with richer inputs. It is worth about 7 branches per decision here. Re-run on 11 Nov 2026 from commit 4c3326e: identical to every reported digit.
claims.formula: gate condition 3: critic error < 32-branch Monte Carlo error

claims.statement: Confirmatory version of H1: 10 seeds, pre-registered, interquartile mean with stratified bootstrap intervals, Holm correction, learned (MAPPO) teams. Refuted if executed-branch training is no better than on-policy training.
Phase 2: audits that agents cannot detect keep blame shifts below 0.1 R in adversarial tasks. Refuted if large shifts survive.
